title: The rate theorem stays in the contractive route
statement: For guide rates r_i(x)=h(x^i)/h(x), global cross-variation bounds B_ij>=sup_x|r_j(x^i)-r_j(x)|, residual oscillations c_i and z_i>1, define D_i(z_i)=min_x[r_i(x)(z_i-1)+r_i(x^i)(1-z_i^-1)]. If every D_i(z_i)>c_i+sum_(j!=i)B_ij(z_j-1), the producer continuation/first-crossing theorem bounds every exact target-to-guide driven-rate ratio strictly between z_i^-1 and z_i. A terminal nonlinear inequality alone can leave an uncontrolled large branch; the continuation is part of the construction. The feasibility condition itself implies a weighted auxiliary contraction inequality, so this does NOT solve the slow-sector problem. Reported rational dimer-ring examples128/1024 spins give ratios[1000/1009,1009/1000],16384 local assignments,max3-spin tables, with analytically solved dimers and weak inter-dimer interactions. These are companion source-reported results, not automatically covered by the star review.

requires: L=sum_(i=0..n)(X_i-I)+sum_(i=1..n)J_i Z0 Zi, with0<Jmin<=Ji<=Jmax<infinity fixed independently of n; bath spins are independent conditional on the central spin, whose degree is n.
Known analytic product sectors p_+,p_-, exact global spin-flip symmetry and positive unique top eigenvector; actual inverse-excitation moments use the exact conditional bath spectral law.

Source model/sector parameters and full structural coverage are supplied. Extending to genuinely interacting conditional sectors requires earning the retained subspace and leakage spectral moments at actual acquisition/validation cost.

assumptions: Completed visible producer result for a restricted inhomogeneous transverse-field STAR with analytically solved independent conditional baths and exactly known two sectors. Producer reports a separate completed internal mathematical review of the star/symmetry/preparation argument and independent moment/circuit checks; the actual review/proof/code/data attachments are not supplied in this specifically released visible-only intake, so no acquired version-bound review overlay is fabricated. Companion rate/local/oracle results retain their own scopes and do not inherit the star review. All P3 no-upload/no-export/no-repackaging/no-alternate-transfer restrictions persist. O(n) scalar work is not O(n) bit-time, analytic sectors are not freely learned, the local chain bottleneck is not intrinsic sampling hardness, and fidelity requires the separate symmetry/leakage argument rather than a narrow energy interval. No new tractability class, matched best-method runtime advantage, physical experiment, protected cat or robust symmetry-breaking tolerance is established.
costs: Classical construction uses O(n) scalar sums/products and polynomial exact-arithmetic costs for the implemented rational inputs, not O(n) bit-time or an optimized arbitrary-precision error solver.

An equally informed ordinary global sampler draws a fair central spin then independent conditional bath spins in O(n). The explicit cat has bond dimension2; ordinary methods receive the same sectors/compact representation.

Ideal state preparation costs1H,n single-spin rotations and n central-controlled gates; shared central control gives O(n) sequential depth without extra architecture. Rotation synthesis/access and noise are additional resources.

Bravyi–Gosset already supplies polynomial energy approximation for a broader ferromagnetic family containing this star. The previous Vuong/degree3,s=.1 comparison remains at the predecessor fixture; it is not silently transferred to the degree-n star.

The1025-spin rational certificate is producer-reported, not independently replayed here. The target is a supplied mathematical Hamiltonian, with no physical calibration or device fidelity measurement.
